pillar_reactions.evidence: The most enthusiastic pillar response in the batch, and it was the mobility half that did it: 'No, that sounds amazing' and then unprompted, 'The mobility part is big to me because I've watched some of him doing the stretches... it all just, it sounds exactly what I'm looking for.' He connected it to his own problem himself — 'I feel like a [shit]bag for not doing anything. And I've kind of used my shoulder as an excuse. But I could have been doing this type of stuff' — and to his constraint: no gym within 45 minutes, so a home programme with video form checks and a GoPro was the answer he wanted.

He volunteered corroboration rather than merely accepting: an Army friend who lost a lot of weight on one meal a day, described in detail, ending 'so I'm very, very interested in trying that as well.' His diet was already close to carnivore with clean sourcing, so the pillar mostly confirmed what he does. This is also where the clotting disorder surfaced — inside an answer about eating large quantities of garlic — and it passed without a single follow-up question.

The community and group workouts landed harder than the accountability mechanics: 'you had mentioned he'll do some live stuff, jump into the group and get my [ass] handed to me. Like, that puts me back into, like, training. And I miss that [stuff], to be honest. So that's the type of community I like.' The pull for him is a return to a unit training environment, not being chased about missed workouts, and the rep read that correctly.

anchors.raw: six grand for six months of, like, realistic, functional... Like, you know, diet, all this is included. Like, dude, that's a, that's an investment that is worth it. 100%.
anchors.note: The strongest and only unprompted price endorsement in the batch, delivered seconds after the number was named and without a single objection. He followed it with 'my goal is to look back and be like, that's the best six grand I ever spent.' Whatever else went wrong on this call, price was never in question.

anchors.raw: The only gyms that are here is a YMCA... it's the size of a typical maybe three-bedroom house... Or Anytime Fitness, but the one that's here, it's like 98% all cardio for older ladies. There's no kettlebells.
anchors.note: Geography removes the substitute entirely. He also rules out driving: 'I'm not driving 45 minutes to go to a gym.' A home programme is not competing against a $40 gym membership here, it is competing against nothing, which is the most favourable price position in the batch.

anchors.raw: there's a dude that I do watch... I think it's Athlean-X... But that's all gym [stuff]. That's not what I can do.
anchors.competitor: Athlean-X and Chris Heria on YouTube
anchors.note: Free alternatives were named and dismissed by the prospect himself on suitability rather than by the rep on value — Athlean-X because it needs a gym, calisthenics because he does not want bodyweight only. A latent anchor that never activated.

anchors.raw: the current limit is 25... I've never really used credit much. Literally, I have one credit card, so I would need to call USAA and request an increase on my card.
anchors.note: Not a value or affordability anchor — a mechanical ceiling. A $2,500 limit against a $6,000 price, on a buyer who deliberately avoids credit. It is the only thing that stopped this deal, and it was solvable with a seven-minute phone call the prospect volunteered to make twice.

unmet_demand.want: A safe starting kettlebell weight given an untreated shoulder injury, and an equipment list he could buy against before onboarding
unmet_demand.why_unmet: He asked three separate times and was routed to the onboarding call each time. He had already done his own research in Trevor's comment sections and found 12 kg, and wanted to know whether that was too much for a compromised shoulder. He also wanted to buy a steel mace and floor mats and had no guidance. A one-page starting-equipment and starting-weight sheet would have answered all of it.

unmet_demand.want: A way to bring his 16-year-old son into the training
unmet_demand.why_unmet: He raised it four times — training together, the son joining a group workout, whether he would get videos to pass on. The answer each time was an informal 'I'm sure you'd be fine.' There is no family option, no second seat, no policy on minors in group sessions, and no stated position on whether coaching content can be shared. This was one of his two stated motivations.

unmet_demand.want: Confidence that ballistic loaded training is safe with a hereditary clotting disorder and an unimaged shoulder injury
unmet_demand.why_unmet: He did not know to ask, because the disorder never registered as relevant to anyone on the call. The programme has no screening step, no clearance requirement and nobody qualified to assess it. Flagged for a human rather than scored as a gap the rep could have closed.

unmet_demand.want: To pay in full immediately once his credit limit was raised
unmet_demand.why_unmet: He offered twice to make a seven-minute call to his bank and was steered instead toward a partial $2,000 charge because the rep had a following appointment. There is no process for holding a warm buyer over a short payment delay — no invoice, no link, no hold — so the whole transaction depended on the rep and prospect both being free at the same moment.
